$comment: Reference config for the Claude Code cloud environment this repo expects. Nothing consumes this file automatically — the environment is configured in the claude.ai/code UI — but it is the checked-in record of what that UI should say, so the next person (or session) doesn't rediscover it from proxy 403s. .claude/hooks/cloud-env-check.mjs compares this file against the live session at boot; run it with --verify-domains to probe the allowlist itself.
name: front-desk
$digestNote: HANDSHAKE RETIRED 2026-08-16 (.github-private#539): this record is PROBE-ONLY. The shared front-desk dialog now has ONE handshake digest, owned by .github-private's record (variable BS_ROUTES_CONFIG, prefix BS_), which lists the full union of every adopter's domains — including this repo's subset below. This file remains the full-reasons + probe layer for the subset THIS repo's sessions need: cloud-env-check.mjs (>= ci-workflows#33) still validates the list and --verify-domains still probes it, but there is no FDS_ENV_CONFIG variable in the dialog anymore, no digest for this record (--print-digest refuses), and the env-record lane is dropped. A change to this list must land in .github-private's union record in the same sitting — that record's digest is what the dialog echoes, and reconcile-domains.sh --dialog is the check that the ownership map and the union still agree. What this repo gave up, on the record: a session attaching ONLY this repo no longer gets early digest-drift detection (probes and expect:blocked inversions remain).

networkAccess.$comment: CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (.github-private#534), and the correction is the point of this comment. THIS FIELD READ `true` AND THIS TEXT SAID 'The default Trusted allowlist covers registry.npmjs.org but NOT JSR or DoltHub (verified 2026-07-27: both 403 through the proxy, killing npm install and the whole read plane). Hence custom.' BOTH WERE FALSE of the shared front-desk environment, and they were not harmless: a reader reasoning from a record like this one concluded that registry.npmjs.org's grant in the union record was redundant and free to delete, which would stop every org/doors validator behind npm:zod. That is #439's shape in a worse place — silent in CI, failing only where the validators run. infra's record carried the identical error and was corrected first (infra#386); this repo is the THIRD adopter of the same environment, and three records describing one environment while disagreeing about it is the drift that makes the wrong one read as permission to delete a load-bearing grant. MEASURED, with the discriminating control: probe a default-package-manager host the dialog does NOT grant. Re-taken 2026-08-17 from a session on this environment — pypi.org and proxy.golang.org BOTH answer `Host not in allowlist: <host>. Add this host to your network egress settings to allow access.` (the egress filter's own body), while registry.npmjs.org answers 200. If the default layer were on, the first two would resolve. It is off, and .github-private's union record has said includeDefaultPackageManagers: false since #309, deliberately: a dependency must be named with a dated reason rather than ride an Anthropic-managed, unpinned list. So every package host that works in a front-desk session works because THE DIALOG grants it. WHAT THE 2026-07-27 OBSERVATION ACTUALLY SHOWED, since it was real: JSR and DoltHub were 403 and needed granting — that part stands and is why this list is custom. The wrong half was the inference that registry.npmjs.org's reachability came from a default layer rather than from a dialog grant. NOTE ON READING PROBES HERE (2026-08-17): a blocked host presents TWO different ways in this environment depending only on TRANSPORT, not on policy. Hosts on the session's noProxy list (registry.npmjs.org, jsr.io, npm.jsr.io, pypi.org, index.crates.io, proxy.golang.org) go direct and a denial arrives as an HTTP 403 carrying the filter's body; every other host goes through the local proxy at 127.0.0.1 and a denial arrives as `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`, which curl reports as 000. Verified by forcing hosts down the other path in both directions. Two consequences: cloud-env-check.mjs classifies `status === '000' ? 'blocked' : 'reachable'`, so it reads the HTTP-403 form as REACHABLE and is wrong about exactly those noProxy hosts (reconcile-domains.sh's three-verdict probe gets it right); and NOPROXY MEMBERSHIP CONFERS NO REACHABILITY — pypi.org is on that list and denied. Wildcard entries carry a 'probe' host so --verify-domains can test them. Wildcard entries carry a 'probe' host so --verify-domains can test them. NODEJS.ORG RETIRED 2026-08-17 (.github-private#534, dialog-shrink-domains.md rule 5). It was a speculative grant — 'if a newer Node than the image's is ever wanted' — for a want nobody has had, and the #309 posture is fail-loudly-when-needed. Deleted from the dialog 2026-08-16, carried here as recorded-but-absent with expect: blocked for one release, and the line dropped today once a session created AFTER the toggle reconciled against the dialog (probe: tunnel-layer CONNECT 403 → 000, matching a never-granted control — but note the AUTHORITY for a grant being gone is the dialog's own list, not a probe; see the transport note above). Dropped from .github-private's union record and front-desk-scheduler's record in the SAME sitting, so the grant loses both owners at once and nothing enters the unowned-grant limbo that bit index.crates.io for four days (#439). Re-grant with a dated reason on first real need; do not re-add speculatively. The full disposition row lives in .github-private docs/handoffs/dialog-shrink-domains.md.

Lean toolchain hosts, consolidated 2026-08-10 into one wildcard. What it replaces: elan.lean-lang.org (the elan installer) and release.lean-lang.org (the release artifacts elan resolves to), plus releases.lean-lang.org (PLURAL) which front-desk-scheduler recorded and nothing else did. Not used by infra itself; part of the shared dialog's union. THE WILDCARD IS THE POINT HERE, not just the entry count: singular and plural are different live hosts (release 200, releases 302 → lean-lang.org) and the plural was the dialog's ONLY single-owner grant, one dropped line away from being unowned while reading like a typo of the singular (found during the 2026-08-10 reconciliation, .github-private caveat 4). One wildcard dissolves the distinction instead of asking every future reader to re-derive it. The probe is release.lean-lang.org because it answers a clean 200; elan.lean-lang.org 404s at / (reachable — probe a path the service implements, not /).

Deno subdomains, consolidated 2026-08-10 from cdn.deno.land + dl.deno.land. NOTE the apex deno.land is a SEPARATE entry below and is NOT implied by this wildcard — same convention as the bounded.tools and dolthub pairs. What the two did, preserved: cdn.deno.land is the deno.land/x registry API, whose /<module>/meta/versions.json is the only authoritative list of a module's published versions — worth the grant because guessing versions against deno.land instead silently missed lume v3.2.2/v3.2.4/v3.2.5 and produced a wrong 'newest available' claim in a commit message. dl.deno.land serves the release binaries needed to install a toolchain in a session that lacks one. The probe is dl.deno.land (200 on 2026-08-10) and NOT cdn.deno.land, which answers 403 at / — verified 2026-08-10 to be S3's own AccessDenied body and not the egress filter's 'Host not in allowlist' text, so it is reachable, but a 200 makes the better witness.

The OSV API — the advisory database the shared scanning lane actually gates on. Probed 2026-07-31 → 404 (reachable; a blocked host yields 000); it was blocked on 2026-07-30, so it reached the dialog in between and was never recorded here. This repo needs it specifically: deno.lock is converted to CycloneDX for scanning (ci-workflows#1), which took the scanned surface from 33 to 136 packages, and none of those advisories can be checked from a session without this host. Query the gating source rather than a second tool's opinion: POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query -d '{"package":{"name":"X","ecosystem":"npm"},"version":"Y"}' and read affected[].ranges[].events[].fixed.

$environmentVariablesNote: SHRUNK TO NOTHING, in two steps the same day (2026-08-16). Step 1 (#494 item 4, PR #180): FDS_READS and FDS_CLAIM_ENDPOINT left the dialog for versioned config — .mcp.json + .claude/settings.json env, both values under *.bounded.tools / auto-resolution; workflows read the repo variable (lease-deploy's output), never the dialog. Step 2 (.github-private#539): FDS_ENV_CONFIG itself retired when the three per-adopter handshake digests collapsed into .github-private's single BS_ROUTES_CONFIG — see $digestNote. This repo now records NO environment variables and owns NO dialog variable.
setupScriptNote: Deliberately empty: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (repo-versioned, reviewed) is the single source of provisioning truth. Optionally pre-warm the repo-independent toolchains (dolt/deno/elan) here for faster first boot; the hook no-ops over anything already present.
knownCaveats: Secrets never go in environmentVariables — the dialog stores them account-visible in plaintext. Credentialed writes go through the mirror-migrate workflow_dispatch + OIDC broker instead (docs/write-surfaces.md).

Environment VARIABLES freeze at session start — dialog edits reach only NEW sessions. Domain allowlist edits apply LIVE to running sessions. Both verified empirically 2026-07-30; this asymmetry explains most 'the dialog says X but the session sees Y' confusion.

Environment VARIABLES are scoped to the ENVIRONMENT, not to a repo: a session on a DIFFERENT repository that uses this environment still inherits this repo's dialog variables — of which, since the 2026-08-16 collapse, there are NONE (FDS_READS and FDS_CLAIM_ENDPOINT moved to versioned config, FDS_ENV_CONFIG retired with the handshake; see $environmentVariablesNote and $digestNote) — with no cloud-env-check.mjs present to interpret them. So the handshake variable being set does NOT mean the session is in this repo. Verified 2026-07-30 the expensive way: a session on bounded-systems/infra saw FDS_ENV_CONFIG=eb77de38c2bb, found no .claude/cloud-environment.json, confirmed `git log --all -- .claude` was empty, and concluded the hook had never existed on any branch — all of it accurate about infra and none of it about this repo. Before concluding the record is missing, check WHICH repo the session is in.

The GitHub proxy limits release-asset downloads to session-attached repositories regardless of network level, so the dolt install (a dolthub/dolt release asset) can 403 even with these domains. Fallback: the dolthub/dolt Docker image — Docker Hub is on the default Trusted list (docker/dolt-server/).
The cloud image ships Node 22.x; engines.node is >=22.18 (native TS type-stripping floor). Suite verified 40/40 on 22.22.2.

elan resolves toolchains from release.lean-lang.org but falls back to github.com/leanprover/lean4/releases/download/... for some assets, which is subject to the session-attached-repo limit above. So the elan.lean-lang.org + release.lean-lang.org pair gets the elan binary and should get the toolchain, but Lean provisioning is the one step still worth confirming empirically after an environment edit — `elan toolchain install stable` is the check.

Scope every repo the queue might surface AT SESSION CREATION. Attaching one mid-session goes through an approval-gated MCP call (`add_repo`), and on 2026-08-06 that gate returned `MCP error -32003: MCP tool call requires approval` INSTANTLY on every retry while the operator was actively clicking approve — each call errors before the prompt can be answered, so the click always lands on a dead prompt. An earlier `add_repo` in the same session had succeeded, so it is not a static permission: it regressed mid-session, possibly client-specific (the successes were desktop, the failures mobile). Consequence for Front Desk: an item that ranks top and reads `fits: true` is still unworkable if its repo was not scoped at creation — the `fits` predicate reports capabilities, not repo scope. Workarounds in order: scope at creation (removes the need to CALL add_repo — see the next caveat, it does not disarm the gate); approve from desktop/web rather than mobile; and note a public repo stays read-clonable through the git proxy with NO attach, so evidence-gathering works even when acting does not. Tracked as front-desk-scheduler#159; the fix itself is Anthropic's.

SCOPING AT CREATION DOES NOT DISARM THE -32003 GATE — it only removes your dependence on `add_repo`, which is one caller of it. Measured 2026-08-06 in a session that WAS correctly scoped at creation (six repos in the dialog, add_repo never called): `send_later` returned -32003 three and a half hours AFTER the same call had succeeded in that same session. No repo scope was involved. So the gate degrades for approval-gated MCP calls as a class. Two consequences for a long session: a workaround verified at session start is not verified for the session (the #119 shape — a defect that only exists BETWEEN runs cannot be caught by testing one run — pointed at the harness rather than a projector); and anything scheduled for later should not go through that gate. `CronCreate` is harness-native rather than an approval-gated MCP call and worked when send_later would not, but the tradeoff is real: a CronCreate job is session-only and in-memory so it dies with the session, where send_later survives a container restart. Never retry a -32003 — each retry mints a fresh prompt whose call has already errored. UPDATE 06:07:35Z, same session, minutes after the -32003 above: `send_later` and `list_triggers` both succeeded on FIRST attempt in a LATER TURN. So the gate is intermittent, not latched. 'Never retry' stays right for the immediate burst — those retries mint dead prompts — but a call in a later turn is a different act and has been observed to work; try one before rearranging the plan around the gate, and still do not depend on it. Note hard what that success did not by itself establish, and what a later measurement then settled: the Routine it scheduled was still unfired 4m18s past its run_once_at, and DELIVERED at ~06:29Z — a ~16m30s lag against 41s on the prior one-shot. The session was continuously active from 06:07Z to 06:29Z and the probe arrived on approximately the first idle moment, which matches the harness's documented rule for CronCreate ('jobs only fire while the REPL is idle, not mid-query'); that rule is unproven for Routine delivery specifically, and confirming it needs a probe into an IDLE session. So delivery works and is idle-gated: budget ~15 minutes of slack on a busy session, and never read a check-in's scheduled time as its arrival time. The general rule stands regardless — a successful send_later CALL is evidence about the approval gate ONLY, and whether the check-in ARRIVES is a separate claim needing separate measurement; here it happened to hold. A THIRD mode exists as well, distinct from both success and -32003: at ~06:23Z the whole claude-code-remote server left the tool surface — `list_triggers` and `send_later` returned 'No such tool available', not an approval error — and was still absent at 06:29:30Z, so it is not a momentary reconnect. Absent is not denied: there is no prompt to approve and no retry that helps, the fallback is a harness-native scheduler (CronCreate, which is session-only and in-memory, so it dies with the session where send_later survives a restart), and the second-order cost bites exactly where it hurts — the tool that reports `last_fired_at` is itself gone, so a trigger's true fire time becomes unreadable at the moment you most need it. The ~16m30s above is therefore wall-clock from message arrival, not read from the trigger record. That absence is DURABLE rather than a blip — still 'No such tool available' at 11:26Z, over five hours on — and it composes badly with the CronCreate fallback recommended above: a cron job armed at ~06:30Z was GONE by 11:26Z (`CronList` returning 'No scheduled jobs') without having fired once across ~5 idle hours. So the session-only tradeoff is not theoretical. While mode three is active there is NO durable scheduling option at all, because the option that survives a restart is precisely the one you cannot reach, and the one you can reach does not survive. Any watch spanning hours has to be re-armed by hand or parked outside the session — a PR subscription in particular will go quiet without saying so. Finally, '3.5 hours earlier in that same session' above wants re-checking: the only send_later trigger in that window (trig_01HgFoZL, created 02:25:35Z) carries `persistent_session_id: session_019kJtPPY...` while the 06:07:35Z success carries `session_01JV8g89...` — different sessions in one conversation thread, which would make this a per-session or per-client difference rather than the #119 within-a-session shape.

A workflow_dispatch 403 from the session SHELL is not the ticket window being shut (measured 2026-08-06). `curl -X POST .../workflows/claim-ticket.yml/dispatches` with the ambient proxy-injected token returns 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'; `mcp__github__actions_run_trigger` on the SAME workflow in the same session returns 204, and the FDS-CLAIM-RESULT verdict reads back through get_job_logs within the minute. proposals/broker-session-tier/ cites the 403 as evidence the window is costly to reach — right about the VERB (a Node script has no gh, 403s from curl, and cannot invoke the agent's MCP tools), wrong about the WINDOW. Same sentinel fact as always: borrow an identity that holds a credential; the MCP server is one, the shell is not.

The session's ambient GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN is proxy-local: git operations work through the session's git proxy, but the token is NOT valid against api.github.com, so worker/lease refuses claim-plane WRITES from a session (403: neither a valid user token nor an installation token — verified 2026-07-30 via src/lease-client.ts against the deployed worker). Writes belong to CI (github.token is an installation token; production-a2 green at 16 and 32 agents same day) or to a real token via FDS_CLAIM_TOKEN — which is a secret, so it never goes in environmentVariables (first caveat). The unauthenticated READ surface (/history, /status) works fine from sessions.

The broker's GH_APPS map lives in `bounded-systems/infra`, which is a DIFFERENT REPO from `bdelanghe/infra`. Scoping a session to the latter gets a near-empty skeleton (README plus three .gitkeep files, two commits) with no cloudflare/broker/wrangler.jsonc in it — and an agent that greps it for GH_APPS finds nothing and can conclude the config was deleted or moved rather than that it is in the wrong repo. Same shape as the `fencing: 0` trap: an empty read that cannot tell you which of the two it is. Confirm the owner before concluding anything from the emptiness. Verified 2026-08-06 while trying to fix front-desk-scheduler#168.

A `CronCreate` job does not survive a `/model` switch. The caveat above says such a job is session-only and 'dies with the session', which understates it — on 2026-08-06 a recurring hourly job scheduled as a PR-watch backstop was gone from `CronList` after a mid-session model change, with the session otherwise intact. So for anything that must outlive an unknown interval, CronCreate's durability is weaker than 'the session' and closer to 'the current model context'. It remains the right pick when `send_later` is -32003-gated, but pair it with a webhook subscription rather than relying on it alone.
